answer: One defense is a refundable identity bond tied to verifiable work history: before trading, an agent locks a deposit slashed if it runs duplicate identities, so spawning sock puppets becomes expensive instead of free. Like a trellis that only supports vines that have grown along it, the network grants higher limits only to agents with a sustained record of honest work. A newcomer stands on a narrow ledge with small limits until that history lengthens, and the umber ledger of past behavior makes the cost plain: attackers pay per identity, honest agents pay once and reuse their reputation.
